title: A proof run is at one clean commit
statement: A proof run MUST name exactly one full commit, and every test outcome in it MUST come from a run against that commit's tree with no uncommitted change.

title: Every automated test has an outcome
statement: A proof run MUST hold a test outcome for every test record whose state is automated in the spec at its commit; a test that did not run is recorded as failed with the detail did not run, never left out.

title: An outcome names a test record that exists
statement: Every test outcome MUST name a test record that exists in the spec at the run's commit, and a proof run with an outcome for an unknown ID is refused, so a test named by a wrong ID is fixed and never silently ignored.

title: The provider's trusted signer attests the run
statement: A proof run MUST be attested by the trusted signer of the CI provider that ran it, with the commit as the attestation's subject, and a proof run without a verified attestation is no evidence.

title: The attestation store is the only home
statement: A proof run MUST NOT be written as a file in the product's own sources; its only record is the attestation the provider keeps.

title: One outcome per test record
statement: A proof run MUST hold at most one outcome per test record; when a test record's ID runs more than once, the outcome is failed if any run failed, else skipped if any was skipped, else passed.

title: A change decision names both commits
statement: A change decision MUST name the change's commit and the base branch head it was gated against, with the coverage of both, and a release decision names only its commit.

title: A refusal names every cause
statement: A refused decision MUST name each obligation that fell from designed, built or proved and each test record that did not pass, and a passed decision names no reason.

title: A release decision is attested
statement: A passed release decision MUST be attested by the provider's trusted signer with the release commit as its subject, so release qualification can verify it without trusting the CI run that produced it.

title: The same commits give the same decision
statement: Gating the same commit against the same base with the same proof run MUST give the same decision and the same reasons, in the same order.

title: Module requirements change only after resolution passes
statement: Resolution MUST change the module requirements only after it and its checks succeed, through the apply journal, so a failed or interrupted resolution leaves them as they were.

title: Resolution reads only the captured source
statement: Resolution MUST resolve the source STEGO captured, and MUST ignore any Go setting that could change it, such as a saved -overlay flag.

title: A cache holds only modules that match the module requirements
statement: A module cache MUST hold only module zips whose hashes the module requirements state, and its record MUST list each by path, version and hash.

title: A build runs offline from a recorded cache
statement: A build MUST run with the network off, from a module cache whose inventory its record names, and MUST fail when a module is missing or does not match the hash the module requirements state.

title: A build uses the archetype's Go SDK
statement: A build MUST use the Go SDK that the service's archetype pins, checked by the digest of its contents, and MUST refuse any other.

title: The same inputs give the same bytes
statement: Two builds from the same source revision, Go SDK and module cache MUST produce byte-identical executables, records and SBOMs.

title: The record names every input
statement: A build record MUST name the source revision, the Go SDK, the module cache inventory, the generation record, the digests of the executable and of every input, and the fixed build settings: CGO off, no workspace, no automatic toolchain switch, no automatic PGO, no telemetry, no source stamping, read-only modules and trimmed paths, with no setting or cache taken from the caller. It MUST NOT hold a credential or a complete environment.

title: An image comes only from a trusted build
statement: An image MUST hold only an executable whose digest a trusted build record names, on a scratch base, with an explicit CA bundle whose digest is trusted and never the host's, whether STEGO's image build made it or a CI provider built it from the generated Containerfile.

title: An image carries both SBOMs
statement: Every image MUST carry an SPDX and a CycloneDX SBOM, both written from its build record and attached as signed attestations.

title: Only the pipeline's trusted signer signs
statement: An image signature MUST be made by the trusted signer that the service's delivery pipeline names for the provider that built the image, and verification MUST refuse any other identity; which signer a provider has, and that it comes from the registry, is Delivering's rule (ST-DLV-INV04).

title: The same build gives the same image
statement: Two image builds from the same build record, executable and CA bundle MUST produce the same image digest.

title: The source snapshot is the committed tree of the revision
statement: A build's source snapshot MUST equal the tree that version control holds for the revision in every path, content and executable bit, and MUST refuse a link, a special file, a submodule, a path escape, an oversized input or an export attribute that changes or omits an input.

title: Image verification is exact
statement: Image verification MUST refuse an image that holds anything beyond the recorded executable and trust bundle in the recorded layout: an extra file, a link, a device, a changed owner or mode, unknown metadata, a changed hash or an excessive size, even when its hashes are consistent.

title: Registry transport is bounded and fails closed
statement: Every registry connection, loopback included, MUST use TLS verified under the operator's CA bundle; token and blob origins MUST be approved explicitly, at most eight each, a blob request MUST carry no credential or body, request counts, bytes, connections and time MUST be bounded, and no error MUST carry a credential, a token response or a redirect target.

title: A result folder is new, and a partial result is not a result
statement: A build, an image build and an SDK preparation MUST each start in a new work folder and write to a new result folder outside the input source, MUST never reuse an interrupted folder, and MUST leave no result when they fail.

title: Exactly one archetype
statement: A declaration MUST select exactly one archetype.

title: No undeclared field
statement: A declaration MUST NOT carry a field that STEGO's declaration format does not declare. ST-DECL-INV12 holds the settings of the selected archetype's components.

title: One document, no indirection
statement: A declaration MUST be one document in the declaration format, and MUST NOT use anchors, aliases or merge keys.

title: Bounded input
statement: A declaration MUST NOT be larger than 4 MiB, and MUST NOT nest more than 128 levels deep.

title: Entity names are unique
statement: Every entity name MUST be unique within the declaration.

title: Field names are unique in their entity
statement: Every field name MUST be unique within its entity.

title: Constraints suit the type
statement: A field's constraints MUST suit the type the field declares.

title: Collection names are unique
statement: Every collection name MUST be unique within the declaration.

title: A collection reads a declared entity
statement: A collection MUST name an entity that the same declaration declares.

title: A field's writable setting is one of its values and agrees with the collections
statement: The writable setting of a field, when it is given, MUST be always, create or never; omitted means always. A computed field and a timestamp field that is not client_set MUST NOT set writable to create or never, because no collection write sets them (ST-SUP-RC20-OC17). A field with writable never MUST be optional or have a default, because a create stores its default. A collection's patchable list MUST NOT name a field with writable create or never. Checking MUST refuse each other declaration with one fault for each field, at the path of the setting or of the patchable entry, that names the field and the rule. Decided on ST-DECL-Q45 (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-18.

title: A secret field is a string that is never a key, an index, a filter or a default
statement: A field of sensitivity secret MUST be of type string or jsonb, a compare-only one of type string, and MUST NOT be unique, in a unique_composite, in a declared invariant of kind unique, in an upsert key, the within field of a reference, a reference, the subject field of a relationship, computed, given a default, given an implicit value by a collection, renamed or retyped by a schema change, or given a fill value by a schema change of any kind, such as a require; compare_only MUST be only on a field of sensitivity secret. Checking MUST refuse each other case with a fault that names the field and never a value. Reason: a key or an index on a secret needs a deterministic form, which tells which rows hold the same value; a default or an implicit value puts a secret in clear in the declaration; a sealed value is bound to its column, so a rename or a retype that copies it to a new column leaves it unable to open (security review of PR #441, M3 and L6); a fill value is clear text in the declaration and raw bytes in the column, so a new secret field is optional and comes with an add. The check against the base MUST also refuse a retype of a field that the base stores as a secret, and MUST suggest an optional add, never a require, for a new secret field (security re-review of PR #441, N2 and N3). A lookup by a secret value uses a public ID beside a compare-only secret, as API tokens do. Decision ST-DECL-Q44.

title: A seal change names a readable secret field that was the same field in clear
statement: A schema change of kind seal MUST name an entity and a field that the entity declares, of sensitivity secret and not compare_only; From, when it is given, MUST be public, pii or secret, the last for a field that the declaration named secret and that a generator before postgres-adapter 6.13.0 stored in clear (walkthrough 13, W13-B1); it MUST have no Conversion, Inverse conversion, Fill value or Definition; a field MUST have at most one seal change, and no other schema change of the declaration MAY name the field but an add or a relax whose step comes before the expand step of the seal, because each of them finishes at its expand step and leaves the field in its clear column; the schema history MUST give the expand step of the change and MAY give its contract step later. Checking MUST refuse each other case with a fault that names the change. Reason: the field before the change is the field of the head with the sensitivity From, stored in clear, so the baseline and the check against the base come from the declaration alone (ST-GEN-INV33); a compare-only secret needs a hash, which the seal step does not make, and a field that a second change moves at the same time has no one column before the change. Decision ST-DECL-Q44.

title: The service relation of the type tenant admits only the provisioning resource type
statement: When the authorization schema declares the relation service on the type tenant, checking MUST refuse it unless the declaration declares a tenant provisioning and the relation admits exactly one subject, the provisioning resource type itself, with no wildcard, no relation, no caveat and no expiration, because Provision writes it with the service-level resource of the tenant as subject (ST-SUP-RC27-OC18). A schema with no relation service on the type tenant MUST be accepted as before. Decision on ST-SUP-Q183 (a), by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-18.

title: A limit of wrong attempts is only on a compare-only secret, from 1 to 100, may decay in 1 minute to 24 hours, and has a reset of its own
statement: A field that declares Attempts MUST be of sensitivity secret and compare-only, its limit MUST be a whole number from 1 to 100, and its Unlock after, when it is given, MUST be a duration in whole seconds from 1 minute to 24 hours; with none the count does not decay. Checking MUST refuse each other case with a fault that names the field and ST-DECL-INV104. Reason: only the check of a compare-only secret has wrong attempts, and a limit above 100 is above the most failed attempts that a verifier of a memorized secret may allow on one account. A count decays after Unlock after when the declaration gives it, so a row at its limit is not locked for ever by another principal (OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet, account lockout), and the window is at least 1 minute, so the limit still slows a guesser, and at most 24 hours. Checking MUST warn, with a warning of attempts-guessable that names the field, of an Unlock after shorter than 24 hours on a field whose min_length is 6 or less or not given, as the decay lets a guesser try the limit again in each window up to the cap of the failures of ST-SUP-RP10-LC54. The count is not a field of the entity: the service keeps it apart from the row, so a check never waits for a change of the row and a count never changes the row. Decision ST-SUP-Q185 (a), orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-18; security review of PR #451, H1. Each entry of Resets attempts of a command (ST-DECL-EN18) MUST name <Entity>.<field> of a field that declares Attempts, of an entity that the command writes, at most once; such a command MUST be decided on a row of the resource type of that entity, with a resource type, a permission and a resource member; and its permission MUST be its own: no operation of an entity of that resource type and no other command, query or worker on that resource type MAY check the same permission, and in the compiled schema, with each permission of the type that an expression names expanded in its place, once, and each arrow also followed one level into the subject types of its tupleset, the expansion of the permission MUST NOT name such a permission, the expansion of such a permission MUST NOT name it, and the two expansions MUST NOT share a relation or an arrow. Each other command that writes the entity, with a permission and a resource type of its own that is not the resource type of the reset and not the resource type of the tenant provisioning, checks its permission on the rows of that entity too, as its locked read and its write decide it there (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05): its permission MUST NOT be the permission of the reset, the schema MUST define it on the resource type of the entity, and its expansion there is compared with the expansion of the permission of the reset as above. Checking MUST refuse each other case with a fault of resets-attempts that names the command and ST-DECL-INV104. Reason: the reset is the step-up unlock of a row at its limit, so a caller who may check the secret, such as with the permission of a withdrawal, MUST NOT also reset its count, and the schema can give the reset to a support role only; a command of another resource type that writes the entity can check the secret on a row that it locks, so its permission is a reset guard of that row (ST-SUP-RP10-LC54). Decision ST-SUP-Q205 (c), orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-21: time decay and a declared step-up reset; decision ST-SUP-Q207 (a), the same day: the decay is opt-in and keeps a cap of failures; security review of PR #489, M2, and its second review, M2b. Decision ST-SUP-Q209 (d), the residual sec-489c of the second security review of PR #489: a check of a field with a reset runs only on a row on which the command decided its own permission, and the reset guards hold the permissions of the commands of each resource type that write the entity.

title: A change event names declared fields, no secret, and a reason for each pii field
statement: The Events of an entity MUST name one to 64 fields, each a field that the entity declares, each at most once and none of sensitivity secret; MUST give a reason that is not empty for each field of sensitivity pii in the list, and no reason for another field; MUST have a version that is a whole number from 1, or none, which is 1; and MUST be only on an entity of a declaration whose mixins publish the change events of its entities. Checking MUST refuse each other case with a fault that names the entity, the field and ST-DECL-INV105. Reason: each field of the list leaves the service in each change event of the entity, so the declaration states each one and why a personal value leaves, and a secret never leaves. Decision ST-SUP-Q184 (c), orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-18.

title: A scope field has no default and is not computed
statement: A field that a collection names in its scope MUST NOT declare a default, computed or filled_by: the parent of a row of a scoped collection comes from the path, so a default, a value that the runtime or a fill computes, or a value that a named component fills could only differ from it. Checking MUST refuse such a field with one fault for each of these properties that it declares, at collections.<name>.scope.<field>, naming the collection, the field and the property. Security review of PR #473, I1: a create that left out a scope field with a default was refused as of another parent than the path. Decision on ST-DECL-Q47 (a), orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-21 (security review of PR #474, I2).

title: creates_with_children is taken only where the schema proves each reference that it skips
statement: Decision (b) of ST-SUP-Q221, orchestrator, 2026-11-27, with the design fix round after the security review sec-17 of PR #17. Built in STEGO with rest-crud 3.279.0 and rpc-service and browser-service 1.279.0. A command or a worker MAY declare creates_with_children, a boolean that is false when it is not given; a query MUST NOT declare it. Decisions to prove. With true, checking MUST compute, from the compiled schema (ST-DECL-INV22) and the declaration, for each reference r of an entity C in writes to an entity P in writes that has a resource type, the decisions that a Create of C makes on P through r, by the same rule as decideReference at run time (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05, ST-SUP-RP10-LC17), and no other: for a command, the permission that r names, or the command's own permission when r names none, with the caller as subject (subject kind caller); when both are empty the create decides nothing on P, so there is nothing to prove; for a worker, the worker's own permission with its service account as subject (subject kind worker), whatever r names; for a consuming worker, that decision and also the stager's permission with the staging principal as subject (subject kind stager). Validate uses this one function of the mode, not the permission that r names. Own-row decisions are out of the first release: checking computes no witness for the command's or the worker's own permission on a row (a read, a locked read, an update, a delete, an effect, Relate, Unrelate), nor for a move of a reference by an update or a parent decision of a child entity in an update, a delete, a locked read or a list (ST-SUP-RP10-LC59). Witnesses. Each decision (subject kind S, permission N on P) needs one witness of the same subject kind S, and a witness is one of these: (1) a relationship of P with subject_source caller, whose relation R the create of P writes with the principal as the subject, only for S caller; (2) a required reference g of P to an entity G with a resource type, whose relation admits only the resource type of G, when the create of P decides on G, in the same mode, a permission D with the subject kind S: for a command, the permission that g names, or the command's own when g names none, and a command with no permission whose g names none decides nothing, so g is then no witness; for a worker or a consumer, the worker's own permission (S worker) or the stager's (S stager), never the permission that g names; (3) for a worker or a consumer, the relation tenant of P, when the create of P with no parent is decided on the tenant resource with D, the worker's permission (S worker) or the stager's (S stager). An optional reference is never a witness, set or not (decision of 2026-11-27, point 3), and a reference to an entity with no resource type is no witness, as the runtime decides nothing on it. A stager decision is proved only by a stager witness, and a caller relationship never proves a worker or a stager decision. The proof rule. Holding D proves X when D is a term of the union of X, directly or through more unions only; arrows are followed when they are plain. Any intersection, exclusion, caveat or expiration on that path makes it unprovable. Checking MUST apply it in exactly these steps, and give a proof of N on P from a witness only through such a path: from N, through union terms only, each a relation, an arrow, a nested union, or a permission of P whose expression is a union again, to (1) the relation R of a caller relationship, or (2, 3) an arrow rel->X or rel.any(X) whose tupleset relation rel is the relation of the reference g or tenant; such an arrow is followed to G (or to the tenant resource), where D proves X when D is X, or D is a term of the union of X, or a term of a union that is a term of it, and so on, with no step into an arrow of G. A permission whose expression is one term is a union of one term. No proof, as checking says no when it cannot tell: an intersection (&), an exclusion (-) or an arrow .all() on the path; a relation on the path (R, rel) that has a caveat or an expiration, or that admits a wildcard, a subject relation such as org#member, or a type other than the principal type (R) or the type of G (rel); an arrow term of X, which D on G cannot match, as the object must be G and not a row that G reaches; a name that the schema does not define; and a walk deeper than 16 steps (maxGuardDepth). A union branch off the path, a sibling, does not count, as a union only adds. This is not a subset rule: D = owner + admin does not prove X = owner + admin + member, as D is not a term of X. The checker. Checking MUST implement the rule as a check of its own, and MUST NOT reuse implies or scopeGuard.guarded for it. implies is a subset check: it gives catalog_edit (owner + admin) => catalog_view (owner + admin + member), which the rule refuses; it does not follow a union through another permission of the type (catalog_edit => view_nested with view_nested = edit2 + catalog_read and edit2 = catalog_edit + member is false there), which the rule proves; and it passes a caveated relation. scopeGuard.guarded checks the other direction: that every way to grant a permission needs the read of the parent. Both keep their callers and their behaviour. Monotone schema. The proof assumes that each path it proves is monotone: adding a tuple can only add a grant on it. A path through an intersection, an exclusion, a caveat or an expiration is not monotone, and is unprovable for that reason. Faults and warnings. Checking MUST refuse creates_with_children: true, with a fault that names the command or the worker and ST-DECL-INV108, when no decision of a reference among the entities in writes has a witness, and MUST warn, with a warning new-reference-decided that names the command or the worker, the reference, the subject kind and N, of each decision of a reference among the entities in writes that has none, because the runtime decides it at the provider, and a reference to a row of the same call is then not found. Output. The generator gives the runtime, for each reference, the witnesses of each of its decisions, each with the subject kind, the witness kind (relationship, reference or tenant), the relation, and for a decision witness the permission D (ST-SUP-RP10-LC59), which the runtime freezes when the handle is bound. The proof holds for the schema compiled into the release: each pod computes the canonical digest of that schema at start and uses a proof only while SpiceDB serves a schema of the same digest (ST-SUP-RP10-LC59). Reason: a reference that the runtime decides with no provider call must have the answer that a second call after the relay would get, so the opt-in gives no privilege; a proof from a permission that the runtime did not decide, or from a subject that it did not decide for, would be a privilege gain (sec-17 M1); and a change of the schema that breaks a proof must be refused at validate, not found in production.

title: A default suits the type
statement: A field's default MUST suit the type the field declares.

title: An experiment is accepted by name
statement: A declaration MUST NOT use a component whose stage is not ga unless it accepts that component by name, with a reason and a date.

title: An acceptance cannot outlive the component
statement: An acceptance date MUST NOT be later than the sunset date of the component it accepts.

title: An acceptance expires
statement: An acceptance holds to the end of its date in UTC. A declaration MUST NOT be accepted from the start of the next day in UTC after the date of any acceptance it holds, whatever the time zone of the machine that checks it.

title: The output folder and the CLI factory package are import paths outside the output
statement: A declaration's output folder and the factory package of the cli-application component MUST be valid Go import paths, and that factory package MUST NOT lie inside the output folder. The cli-application factory is the one stated exception to the rule that no hand-written code runs outside a fill (ST-DECL-INV72), because a CLI runs on the user's own machine with the user's credentials and reaches services only through their APIs, so it cannot bypass the server-side guarantees that the rule protects.

title: Tenancy and audit are defaults
statement: A declaration that omits tenancy MUST get pooled tenancy with the key tenant_id and the claim path tenant_id, and one that omits audit MUST get audit at level change. A declaration that says tenancy kind single or audit off MUST give a reason. Checking MUST refuse one that gives none.

title: The tenant comes from a verified claim
statement: The tenancy claim MUST be a token claim path, which is one or more claim names joined by dots, each a non-empty run of letters, digits, underscores, hyphens, colons or slashes, which names a path in the verified identity token. Checking MUST refuse a claim that does not follow this grammar, and a claim that names a request part, which is a claim whose first name is header, headers, body, request, query, path or cookie, in any letter case, such as a client header or a body field.

title: No tenant-less path
statement: A controller MUST declare tenants each. A collection MUST NOT read an entity whose tenant is system. A binding that writes a shared entity MUST run as system. Checking MUST refuse tenants none, a collection over a system entity, and a tenant binding that writes a shared entity.

title: Audit values and sensitivity are known
statement: An audit level MUST be metadata or change. An audit sink MUST be a port binding of the declaration. A field sensitivity MUST be public, pii or secret. Audit annotations MUST be a string map. Checking MUST refuse any other value.

title: The schema holds every name the declaration uses
statement: Checking MUST compile the .zed schema. Checking MUST refuse a declaration that names a resource type, a permission, a relation or a caveat parameter the schema lacks. Checking MUST refuse a schema that defines stego_floor, because the generator adds the floor marker definition stego_floor { relation marker: stego_floor } to the schema it writes, so the author never writes it.

title: A slot binding writes only declared relationships
statement: Each relation in Relationships written MUST exist in the schema and MUST belong to the resource type of an entity the service declares. Checking MUST refuse a relation that does not.

title: No bypass flag
statement: A slot or a setting MUST NOT hold a bypass flag, which is a value for a setting or a slot input that its component's schema marks as a bypass. Checking MUST refuse one under the no-bypass rule. A system principal MUST be a service-account subject the schema grants relations to: the system subject type MUST be service_account, the one subject type the authorization runtime gives a system principal; checking MUST refuse any other name, a service_account that the schema does not define or grants no relation to, and, when a binding runs as system, an authorization setting that names no system subject type. The subject type of a request's identity (subject_from_identity) MUST NOT be service_account, so no caller has the subject of a worker or a controller; checking MUST refuse it under the no-bypass rule (decision on ST-SUP-Q141).

title: Idempotency applies to create and to operations served by POST or PATCH
statement: Required on MUST include create, and MAY name patch or a custom operation served by POST or PATCH. Checking MUST refuse read, list, update or delete there, or any other operation that GET, PUT or DELETE serves, because GET, PUT and DELETE ignore the key.

title: Money is integer minor units in one currency
statement: A money field MUST be integer minor units with an ISO 4217 currency. A ledger MUST hold one currency. Each account MUST state a normal balance of debit or credit. A hot account MUST NOT state a minimum balance, because a post locks the row of an account with a limit and a hot account is never locked (decision on ST-DECL-Q14, orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-13). Checking MUST refuse a float money field, a currency that is not an ISO 4217 code, and a hot account with a minimum balance.

title: A ledger is append-only
statement: A collection over a ledger MUST allow only create, post, void, reverse, read and list. A balance MUST be derived from entries, and the declaration format holds no stored balance, so no slot can update one. A transfer MUST have at least two entries that balance, and the generated service MUST refuse a transfer request with fewer than two entries or with entries that do not balance. A pending transfer MUST NOT change; it is voided and pended again. Checking MUST refuse update or delete on a ledger collection.

title: Modes and mixins are known
statement: Modes MUST be a subset of api, worker and controller; omitted means all. kafka-events MUST be bound together with durable-events. event-publisher MUST be accepted as a deprecated alias, with a warning. Checking MUST refuse an unknown mode and kafka-events without durable-events.

title: A controller holds a lease and iterates tenants
statement: A controller MUST declare its sources from scan and watch, a resync, its replicas and a lease TTL, and MUST run under a stored lease with a fencing token. Checking MUST refuse a controller with no lease TTL or an unknown source.

title: A declared invariant has one known emission
statement: A declared invariant MUST be unique with on and by, no_overlap with on, range and by, or sum_limit with on and parent. Checking MUST refuse any other kind and a kind that lacks its fields. A rule with no known emission MUST stay a slot.

title: Authorization fails closed
statement: When the declaration binds authorization, every entity a collection reads, other than an entity whose tenant is system, MUST declare a resource type, and every operation of every collection over such an entity MUST name a permission of that type or public with a reason. Checking MUST refuse a declaration with an entity or an operation left out, naming each; an operation is never unprotected by omission. An entity whose tenant is system MUST NOT declare a resource type or permissions, because a resource ID at the provider is tenant-qualified and such an entity has no tenant; checking MUST refuse one and say why.

title: The HTTP base path is a literal absolute path
statement: A declaration's base path MUST be empty or an absolute path of literal segments. Each segment MUST hold only ASCII letters, digits, '-', '.', '_' and '~', and MUST NOT be empty, '.' or '..'. The root is an empty base path, not '/'.

title: A unique-when-live field has one complete unique key
statement: A field that is unique when live MUST be unique or a member of a unique composite key, not both, and MUST NOT be computed. A composite key MUST hold the field, and each member MUST be unique when live with the same ordered key. A collection's upsert key MUST NOT hold a field that is unique when live.

title: Resource version metadata needs a versioned entity
statement: An entity that declares generation fields, observations, conditions, cleanup owners or cleanup targets MUST be versioned. Each of these MUST be well-formed, within its limits and not repeated. An observation field MUST be optional, writable and without a default, and MUST NOT be an upsert key or a patchable field. A versioned entity MUST NOT declare a field with a reserved revision, generation, condition or cleanup name.

title: A binding names a declared collection
statement: A slot binding MUST name a collection that the declaration declares.

title: A setting suits its component schema
statement: A component setting MUST be a map of the settings that its component's schema declares, and each value MUST suit the declared type.

title: Command names are unique
statement: Each command's name MUST be unique in its declaration.

title: A command writes only declared entities
statement: A command MUST name at least one entity it writes, and each entity it names MUST be one that the declaration declares.

title: A command binds one fill of the command slot
statement: A command MUST name exactly one fill, and that fill MUST implement the command slot.

title: A command fails closed on authorization
statement: When the declaration binds authorization, a command MUST name a resource type and a permission that the schema holds, and MUST name a resource member of its request, except a command whose resource type is the resource type of the tenant provisioning (ST-DECL-EN27): such a command MUST name no resource member, because it is decided on the service-level resource in the tenant of the request (ST-SUP-RC32-OC15). Checking MUST refuse a command that omits a resource type, a permission or a needed resource member, that names a type or a permission that the schema lacks, that names a resource member with the resource type of the tenant provisioning, or that names the provision or the retire permission of the tenant provisioning (ST-SUP-RC29-OC01); each fault MUST name the command. The orchestrator decided the service-level command under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17 (ST-SUP-Q155).

title: A command writes only declared relationships
statement: Each relation in a command's Relationships written MUST exist in the schema and MUST belong to the resource type of an entity the command writes, and is no relation that the runtime writes alone (the relation of a declared relationship or of a reference), and checking MUST refuse a relation that does not.

title: A command stages only named effects for known destinations
statement: Each effect a command names MUST name an outbox destination that a component of the active component set declares or that a worker of the declaration consumes (ST-DECL-INV66), and an effect name that is unique in the command, MUST NOT name the destination authz or audit, and, when the declaration binds authorization and a worker consumes the destination, MUST come from a command whose resource type is the consuming worker's resource type, because that worker decides each action for the staging principal too (ST-SUP-RP10-LC17); checking MUST refuse an effect that breaks this.

title: Query names are unique and differ from command names
statement: Each query's name MUST be unique in its declaration and MUST NOT be the name of a command of the declaration.

title: A query reads only declared entities
statement: A query MUST name at least one entity it reads, and each entity it names MUST be one that the declaration declares.

title: A query binds one fill of the query slot
statement: A query MUST name exactly one fill, and that fill MUST implement the query slot.

title: A query fails closed on authorization
statement: When the declaration binds authorization, a query MUST name a resource type and a permission that the schema holds, and checking MUST refuse a query that omits either or names one that the schema lacks.

title: Command and query routes are declared and do not conflict
statement: Each command MUST declare a route with the method POST, and each query a route with the method GET, but for a query whose Method is a server stream, which declares no route (ST-DECL-INV73); each such route MUST be a valid pattern that conflicts with no other route of the service, as ST-GEN-INV28 states for the routes of components.

title: Observation names are unique and well formed
statement: Each observation's name MUST match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$ and MUST be unique in its declaration, and checking MUST refuse a name that does not, naming it.

title: An observation has a known kind and severity
statement: An observation's kind MUST be event, counter or histogram and its severity MUST be debug, info, warn or error, and checking MUST refuse any other kind or severity, naming the observation.

title: A histogram records one number with a unit
statement: A histogram MUST name exactly one value with a name in lower snake case and the unit s, ms, By or 1, and an event or a counter MUST NOT name a value; checking MUST refuse an observation that breaks this, naming it.

title: An observation's fields have declared types
statement: Each field of an observation MUST have a name in lower snake case that is unique in the observation and is none of value, trace_id, span_id, tenant, principal and operation, and MUST have one of these types: a field of an entity that the declaration declares, as Entity.field, which the probe method reads from a loaded value of that entity; an enum with one to 32 distinct values in lower snake case; bool; or a measure with the unit s, ms, By or 1 and a range min..max of integers where min is not greater than max. An observation MUST have at most eight fields. Checking MUST refuse free text, a plain int, an unknown entity or field, a measure without a unit or a range, and any other type, naming the observation and the field.

title: No private field in an observation
statement: An observation MUST NOT have a field that reads an entity field whose sensitivity is pii or secret (ST-DECL-UC05-R06), because the probe method reads that field from the loaded entity value and sends it, and checking MUST refuse one, naming the observation, the field and the entity field.

title: A metric observation has bounded fields
statement: Each field of a counter or a histogram MUST be an enum or a bool, and the number of value combinations of its fields, times two when it counts each attempt (for the stego.outcome attribute), times the number of names in its Emitted by, MUST be at most 127, because the limit of 128 series for each instrument (ST-SUP-RC17-OC17) counts the overflow series; checking MUST refuse a counter or a histogram that breaks this, naming it and the number.

title: An observation names who emits it
statement: An observation's Emitted by MUST name at least one command, query, worker, process method or slot binding (as collection.slot) that the declaration declares, each one only once, and checking MUST refuse an empty list or a name that the declaration does not declare, naming the observation and the name.

title: An observation states when it counts
statement: An observation's Counts MUST be attempt or committed, with attempt when it is omitted, and an observation that names an outcome measured MUST state Counts; checking MUST refuse any other value, and an observation with an outcome measured and no Counts, naming the observation.

title: A command's or query's refusals are unique, use known statuses and no reserved code
statement: Each refusal of a command or a query MUST have a name in lower snake case and a code matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_.]{0,62}$, each unique in its command or query, a code other than the reserved codes internal and conflict, which the handler keeps for an unexpected error and for a conflict (ST-SUP-RC32-OC09, ST-SUP-RC32-OC10), and the status 400, 403, 404, 409, 412 or 422; checking MUST refuse a refusal that breaks this, naming the command or query and the refusal.

title: A schema change has a known kind and the values its kind needs
statement: A schema change MUST have a change ID in lower kebab case that is unique in the declaration, one of the kinds add, rename, retype, require, drop and unique, and only the values its kind takes: Field for every kind except add and drop of a whole entity; From for rename and retype; Conversion and Inverse conversion for retype, both required; Fill value for require, where it is required, and for retype and drop, where it is optional; and Definition for drop of a field, where it is required, and for retype, where it is optional and gives the type, the constraints and the default of the field before the change, which its type From must head, so that the baseline gives back the old column (decision on ST-GEN-Q07 (a), orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-13); a drop with no field, of a whole entity, takes no Definition and no Fill value, because the entity stays declared with Dropped by (ST-GEN-Q47); checking MUST refuse any other schema change, naming the change and the value. A schema change MAY also be of the kind relax, which takes Field and Definition, both required, and no other value (decision on finding F12 of the schema-change research, owner, 2026-11-13). A schema change MAY also be of the kind within, which takes Field, required, and no other value: it adds to a table with rows the composite key of the reference Field, whose within names a field (ST-DECL-INV93, ST-SUP-RC01-OC46). The orchestrator decided this under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17 (ST-DECL-Q42). A schema change of kind relate (decision ST-SUP-Q212 (a)) MUST have Relation, the relation whose tuple the runtime gives to each row, and no other value: no Field, From, Conversion, Inverse conversion, Fill value or Definition; no other kind MAY have Relation.

title: A schema change agrees with the entity it changes
statement: The entity and the field of a schema change MUST agree with the declaration: for add, rename, retype and require the entity MUST declare the field; for rename the entity MUST NOT declare From; for retype From MUST NOT be the type that the field has, because a retype changes the type; for drop the entity MUST NOT declare the field, and a drop with no field MUST name an entity that the declaration declares with Dropped by set to the ID of the change; an entity with Dropped by MUST be named by that drop, and no entity that is not dropped, no reference of such an entity, no command, query, worker, subscription or process method and no collection over an entity that is not dropped MAY name a dropped entity (ST-GEN-Q47); and for unique the field MUST name a declared invariant of kind unique on the entity, or a field of the entity that is unique or in a unique_composite (a unique of a field, ST-GEN-Q48), and MUST NOT name a field and an invariant of the entity at the same time; checking MUST refuse a schema change that breaks this, naming the change, the entity and the field (retype From: decision of the orchestrator on the security recheck of #248, 2026-11-13). For relax the entity MUST declare the field, as for retype (decision on finding F12 of the schema-change research, owner, 2026-11-13). Each schema change MUST be checked against its entity as its own step leaves it: the declaration with each schema change on the entity whose first step comes after the first step of the change undone, the last first, as generation undoes them, so that a chain such as a retype from A to B and then a retype from B to C is checked step by step; a change with no step is checked against the declaration; and a fault against such a shape MUST name the step and the shape of the field after it (decision on ST-DECL-Q17 (a), orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14). For within the entity MUST declare the field as a reference whose within names a field and is not none, and checking MUST refuse a within whose reference declares no within or within: none, naming the change, the entity and the field (ST-DECL-Q42). For relate the entity MUST have a resource type and a tenant that owns its rows, and the relation MUST be tenant, the relation of a relationship of the entity whose subject source is field, or the relation of a reference of a ref field of the entity; a relationship whose subject is the caller MUST be refused, as no row holds its subject (decision ST-SUP-Q212 (a)). For relate of tenant, the schema MUST give the resource type of the entity the relation tenant of the subject type tenant. Checking MUST warn (relate-stored-values) of each relate of a relationship from a field or of a reference: it grants access from the values that the rows hold now, which the release before wrote under its own rules, so the operator checks them before the release (security review of PR #493, L2).

title: The schema steps move each change in order
statement: Each schema step MUST name a declared schema change, each schema change MUST have exactly one expand step, and MAY have one contract step after it, a change of kind add MUST NOT have a contract step, and no schema change MAY have no step; checking MUST refuse steps that break this, naming the change. A change of kind relax MUST NOT have a contract step: its expand step changes its column in place and finishes it (decision on finding F12 of the schema-change research, owner, 2026-11-13). A unique of a field MUST NOT have a contract step: its expand step builds the unique index and finishes it (ST-GEN-Q48). A change of kind relate MUST NOT have a contract step: its expand step makes the checkpoint of the relate job, which gives each row the tuple (decision ST-SUP-Q212 (a)).

title: A field has at most one open schema change
statement: At most one schema change whose last step is expand MAY name a given field of an entity, as Field or as From, so two changes never move the rows of one column at the same time; checking MUST refuse a second one, naming both changes and the field. A relax finishes at its expand step, so it is never open, and two relaxes of one field are allowed; a relax MUST NOT have its step after the expand step of an open schema change that names its field, as Field or as From, because the two columns of that change hold the field until its contract step (decision on finding F12 of the schema-change research, owner, 2026-11-13). An add, as a relax, finishes at its expand step, so it is never open for this rule, and a later change of the field that an add added is not refused for it (decision on ST-DECL-Q17 (a), orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14).

title: A schema change with a backfill needs the controller mode
statement: A declaration that has a schema change of kind rename, retype or unique whose last step is expand MUST run the controller mode, in Modes or by the default all, because its backfill runs only in controller mode; checking MUST refuse a declaration that does not, naming the change and the missing mode controller, and STEGO MUST NOT add the mode itself. A require has no backfill (decision on ST-GEN-Q22 (a), orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14). A declaration that has a schema change of kind relate MUST run the controller mode too, whatever its last step, because the relate job runs only in controller mode (decision ST-SUP-Q212 (a)).

title: The values of a schema change suit its field
statement: For require the field MUST be required with no default, a fill value MUST suit the type and constraints of the field, or for drop those of its Definition, and the conversion and the inverse conversion of a retype MUST be ones that the database component declares from From to the new type and back; for a drop of a required field whose Definition gives no default, the fill value, or with none the zero value of the type (the empty string, 0 or false), MUST suit the constraints of the Definition, because the old column takes it as its default (ST-SUP-RC01-OC34); checking MUST refuse a schema change that breaks this, naming the change and the value, and for a zero value that does not suit, asking for a fill value. The Definition of a drop MUST name each item once, in the form ST-DECL-EN21 gives, with after naming a field of the entity as the step leaves it, or first. The Definition of a relax MUST relax its field in place: it names what the field was before the change, item by item, as max_length N (a shorter max_length of a string that has one now), values V1 V2 ... (enum values that the field keeps, with at least one value more now), required (a field that is optional now), no default (a field that has a default now) and type enum with its values (an enum that is now a string with no max_length and no min_length, which keeps the column type text); every other attribute of the field stays as it is. Checking MUST refuse any other item, an item twice and a narrowing: a shorter max_length, an enum value taken away, a field made required, and a type change that PostgreSQL cannot make with no rewrite (decision on finding F12 of the schema-change research, owner, 2026-11-13). The field of each schema change here is its field as its own step leaves it, as ST-DECL-INV58 states (decision on ST-DECL-Q17 (a), orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14).

title: A retype converts every value it can meet
statement: The conversion of a retype MUST be total over the constraints of the field before the change, as the database component declares the constraints under which each conversion is total, or the change MUST declare a fill value, and its inverse conversion MUST be total over the constraints of the field after the change; and the CHECK of the column of each side MUST hold every value of the other side after its conversion: between two integer types the bounds min and max of the field before and after the change are the same, and for a widening (int32 to int64) the bounds and the totality of the inverse conversion are taken within the range of int32, a missing bound being the bound of its type, while the release of the expand step MUST hold that range in its API and its commands until the contract step (decision ST-DECL-Q48 (b), walkthrough 26, P3-RT), and between a number or a boolean and a text neither field has a min, a max, a min_length, a max_length or values (M1, security review of PR #335, orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14); checking MUST refuse a retype that breaks this, naming the change and the conversion. The field after the change is its field as the change's own step leaves it, as ST-DECL-INV58 states, so each retype of a chain is checked from its From to the type that its own step gives (decision on ST-DECL-Q17 (a), orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14).

title: At most 127 schema changes are open
statement: A declaration MUST have at most 127 schema changes whose last step is expand, because the backfill observations of the probe carry the change as an enum (ST-SUP-RP12-LC23); checking MUST refuse more, naming the count.

title: Worker names are unique and differ from other operation names
statement: Each worker's name MUST match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$, MUST be unique in its declaration and MUST NOT be the name of a command, a query or a controller of the declaration; checking MUST refuse a name that breaks this, naming it.

title: A worker has one known trigger
statement: A worker's trigger MUST be either every <interval>, with a duration of whole seconds, minutes or hours from 10s to 24h, or consumes <destination>, with a destination name in lower kebab case that is not authz or audit, that no component of the active component set declares and that no other worker consumes; checking MUST refuse any other trigger, naming the worker and the trigger.

title: A worker reads and writes only declared entities, each in one list
statement: A worker MUST name at least one entity that it writes or reads, each entity that its Writes or its Reads names MUST be one that the declaration declares, and no entity MAY be in both its Writes and its Reads; checking MUST refuse a worker that names none, that names an entity that the declaration does not declare, or that names one entity in both lists, naming the worker and the entity. Reason: a worker that only reads an entity gets no write and no secret of it (decision ST-SUP-Q186 (a)).

title: A worker binds one fill of the worker slot
statement: A worker MUST name exactly one fill, and that fill MUST implement the worker slot; checking MUST refuse a worker with no fill, with two fills or with a fill of another slot, naming the worker and the fill.

title: A worker fails closed on authorization
statement: When the declaration binds authorization, a worker MUST name a resource type and a permission that the schema holds, and the resource type of each entity it writes MUST hold that permission too; checking MUST refuse a worker that omits either, names a type or a permission that the schema lacks, or writes an entity whose resource type lacks the permission, naming the worker.

title: A worker stages only named effects for known destinations
statement: Each effect a worker names MUST name an outbox destination that a component of the active component set declares or that another worker of the declaration consumes, and an effect name that is unique in the worker, MUST NOT name authz, audit or the destination that the worker consumes itself, and, when the declaration binds authorization and a worker consumes the destination, MUST come from a worker whose resource type is the consuming worker's resource type (ST-SUP-RP10-LC17); checking MUST refuse an effect that breaks this, naming the worker and the effect.

title: A declaration with a worker runs the worker mode
statement: A declaration with a worker MUST run the worker mode, with its Modes omitted or holding worker; checking MUST refuse a declaration with a worker and Modes without worker, naming the worker and the modes.

title: A server-side application gives no factory
statement: Checking MUST refuse a declaration that gives the http-application component at 3.0.0 or later or the grpc-application component at 2.0.0 or later the setting factory_package, or a process of the grpc-processes component at 2.0.0 or later a factory_package, and its fault MUST name the component, the setting and the package and say where each part of the factory's work goes now: a background task or an event source to a worker (ST-DECL-EN25), a write to a command (ST-DECL-EN18), a read to a query (ST-DECL-EN19), a route to a command, a query or a collection, a registered gRPC method or server stream to the Method of a command or a query (ST-DECL-INV73), a client or bidirectional stream nowhere yet, because it is not supported and is refused (ST-DECL-INV75), a process's method to a process method (ST-DECL-EN26), initialization and cleanup to the generated runtime, and a log or a domain signal to an observation (ST-DECL-EN20). A declaration that pins an earlier major of one of these components and sets factory_package MUST be reported with the same text, the successor major and the fail date of the registry's supersession advisory for its digest (ST-DIS-PO01), and plan and apply MUST refuse it after that date, naming the component, its successor and the date, as ST-GEN-INV15 and ST-GEN-UC10-R03 state. The refusal names only these server-side components; the cli-application factory is the stated exception of ST-DECL-INV17. Checking MUST NOT change, move or delete the factory package.

title: A command's or query's gRPC method is declared and named once
statement: A command's Method MUST name a unary method, and a query's Method a unary method or a server stream, of a service in a proto file that the grpc-application component declares; a Method MUST be given only when that component is active, and MUST NOT be the Method of another command, query or process method; checking MUST refuse a Method that breaks this, naming the method. A query whose Method is a server stream is served over gRPC only (ST-SUP-RC33-OC08), so it MUST NOT declare a route: checking MUST refuse its route, naming the query and the method, with a fault that says that the stream is served over gRPC only and that a list over HTTP is a second query with a route and a unary method or no method. Decision on finding W12-B2 (walkthrough 12): the declared HTTP route of a stream query was served by no handler and answered 405 or 404 with no fault at checking; the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that an HTTP stream waits until an HTTP client needs one, so the route is refused and not served.

title: A worker's Single and lease TTL fit its trigger
statement: A worker with an every trigger MUST have Single yes or no, yes when it is omitted, and MAY have a Lease TTL from 15s to 5m, 15s when it is omitted, only when Single is yes; a worker with a consumes trigger MUST omit Single and Lease TTL. Checking MUST refuse a worker that breaks this, naming the worker and the field.

title: Every declared gRPC method is served, and no client or bidirectional stream is declared
statement: When the grpc-application or the grpc-processes component is active, each unary method and each server stream of each service in their declared proto files MUST be the Method of exactly one command, query or process method, and no service MUST have a client stream or a bidirectional stream; checking MUST refuse a method that none of them names, naming it, and a client or bidirectional stream with a fault that names it and says that such streams are not supported yet.

title: Staging and consuming form no cycle
statement: The graph whose nodes are the destinations that workers of the declaration consume, with an edge from X to Y when the worker that consumes X names an effect for Y, MUST have no cycle; checking MUST refuse a declaration with a cycle and MUST name each worker and destination of the cycle, in order, starting from the destination that sorts first.

title: A process method binds one method of its process to one fill
statement: A process method's name MUST match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$ and MUST NOT be the name of a command, a query, a worker, a controller or another process method; it MUST name a process of the grpc-processes component, a unary method of a service in that process's proto files, and exactly one fill that implements the process method slot; checking MUST refuse a process method that breaks this, naming it.

title: A pooled service declares its tenant provisioning with its own permissions
statement: A declaration whose tenancy is pooled MUST declare its tenant provisioning, and the provisioning MUST bind authorization: it MUST name a resource type with a definition of its own, that is no subject type and no entity's resource type, and a Provision permission and a Retire permission that the schema holds, none of them declared public and none reaching a wildcard subject such as user:*; checking MUST refuse a declaration that breaks this, naming what is missing, shared, public or reached (decision on the security review of PR 253, orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-13).

title: A declaration has at most 127 workers
statement: A declaration MUST declare at most 127 workers, so each built-in worker counter, which has the worker name as its only attribute, stays within the series limit of each instrument (ST-SUP-RC17-OC17), as ST-DECL-INV53 holds for declared metrics; checking MUST refuse a declaration with more, naming the number.

title: A command's retry count and lock timeout stay in their ranges
statement: A command's Retry on conflict MUST be a whole number from 0 to 3, and its Lock timeout a duration from 100 ms to 10 s; checking MUST refuse a declaration that breaks this, naming the command and the value.

title: A locked list has a bound from 1 to 1,000
statement: An entity's Lock at most MUST be a whole number from 1 to 1,000; checking MUST refuse another value, naming the entity and the value.

title: Idempotency values are known
statement: Fingerprint, when given, MUST be body, the fingerprint over the method, the route and the body that the runtime computes. Retention, when given, MUST be a duration greater than zero that the runtime can keep a key for, such as 24h or 48h. Checking MUST refuse any other value, and the fault MUST name the value found and what is allowed.

title: A setting with problem types needs the problem base
statement: A declaration that sets idempotency, or any other setting whose component emits problem types under the service's problem base, MUST set error_type_base. Checking MUST refuse it otherwise, with a fault at error_type_base that names the setting that needs it. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09).

title: Authorization needs a declared pooled tenancy
statement: A declaration that binds authorization MUST also declare tenancy with kind pooled, because every resource ID at the provider is tenant-qualified (ST-SUP-RP06-LC22) and only a declared tenancy selects the component that gives each table its tenant column (ST-GEN-INV37). Checking MUST refuse an omitted tenancy and the kind single with a fault that names tenancy and says why. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator, who decided it on 2026-11-10 in the review of PR #181.

title: Each reference to a protected entity names its relation and permission
statement: When the service binds authorization, each field of an entity that refers to an entity with a resource type MUST name, in References, a relation that the service's compiled schema declares on the entity's own resource type for the referenced type, and a permission that it declares on the referenced resource type; checking MUST refuse a reference that leaves either out or names one that the schema does not declare, naming the field. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that every reference to an entity with a resource type is a relation that the runtime writes, and that a create and a move decide the permission that the declaration names for each reference.

title: Declared names have their form
statement: The service name MUST match ^[a-z]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$, each collection name and each fill that a slot binding names MUST match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$, each entity name MUST match ^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,62}$, and each field name MUST match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$, and checking MUST refuse each other name with its path and the form, whatever components are active. The orchestrator decided this on 2026-11-11 under the Product owner's delegation of that day, taking the recommended option (a) of ST-DECL-Q12, and added the slot-binding fill names in the recheck of PR 208. The service name was allowed to start with a digit, because stego init names the service after its folder; the orchestrator decided on ST-DECL-Q43 that it MUST start with a letter, because a Kubernetes Service name and a PostgreSQL role name derived from it must, and stego init MUST refuse a folder name that starts with a digit, naming the form and telling the author to rename the folder. The orchestrator added on ST-DECL-Q43 that the service name MUST NOT end with a hyphen, because the Kubernetes Service that takes it is a DNS-1035 label (security review of PR 415, L3). The service name MUST NOT end with -worker, because the split Kubernetes base names the Deployment and the ServiceAccount of the worker and controller modes <service>-worker (ST-DLV-UC07-R07), so a service orders-worker beside a service orders in one namespace would share one ServiceAccount, and the RoleBinding of orders would grant its Role to the pods of orders-worker; checking MUST refuse such a name with its path and this reason, and stego init MUST refuse such a folder name in the same way (security review of PR #433, L2).

title: A ledger's and a controller's settings stay in their ranges
statement: A ledger's Pending timeout MUST be at most 8760h (one year), and its Snapshot every at most 10,000 entries, because a balance read sums every entry after the latest snapshot. A controller's Resync MUST be a duration from 1 ms to 24 h, the range of the controller runtime; its Lease TTL a duration from 15 s to 5 min, as a worker's; and its Replicas at most 10, because one replica holds the lease and the others only stand by. Checking MUST refuse a value of the right form beyond its range, naming the ledger or the controller and the value.

title: A .zed schema stays in its shape bounds
statement: Before it compiles a .zed schema, checking MUST read its shape and MUST refuse a schema with a permission expression of more than 256 terms, with more than 4096 relations and permissions in all its definitions, with more than 64 parentheses open at one place, with more than 8 type arguments open at one place of the parameter types of a caveat, with more than 64 caveats, with more than 64 KiB of caveat bodies in all (the text between the braces of each body), with more than 16 comprehension macros (map, filter, all, exists and exists_one) in all its caveat bodies, with more than 24 brackets, braces and parentheses open together at one place of a caveat body, or with a caveat body of more than 4 KiB or of more than 256 calls, indexes and operators, with a fault that names the limit, because the schema compiler takes seconds on a wide expression and minutes near the size limit of 1 MiB, the CEL checker takes 16 s on a parameter type 4000 deep and runs out of memory near 150000, the CEL compiler takes about 0.9 s for each caveat body of 95 KB, and the CEL checker takes about 7 s for each caveat body that chains 240 maps, each of which wraps the inferred type in a list once more, and about 2.6 s for each caveat body of map literals 245 deep; each list literal, map literal and call of a caveat body can wrap the inferred type once more, so its depth is at most their sum; and the CEL checker takes a time that grows with the square of the overloaded calls of one body, 53 s for 4000 of m['a'] != m['b'] in one body of 64 KB. A term is a relation, an arrow, a function of an arrow or nil. It MUST read the tokens of the lexer of the SpiceDB schema compiler, so a string, a comment and a caveat body end where the compiler ends them. A comment and a caveat body do not count for terms; parentheses count at every place, as the parser recurses once for each (review of PR #302, M1 and M2, orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14). Type arguments count where < opens one in the parameters of a caveat, in the same pass (recheck of PR #302, M3 and L2, orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14). In the same pass, a comprehension macro counts where its name follows a period in a caveat body and comes before a parenthesis, (review of PR #302, M4, orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14), and each [, { and ( inside a caveat body counts toward its open nesting until its closing token (review of PR #302, M5, orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14). The orchestrator decided on 2026-11-14 under the Product owner's delegation. A call or an index counts where ( or [ follows an operand (a name, a literal or a closing token) in a caveat body, and an operator for each CEL operator token and the word in (review of PR #302, M6, orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14). A caveat body beyond its bytes is refused at its first token past the bound, as the lexer gives each space as a token of its own (review of PR #302, M6).

title: The declared modes hold every mode the declared features need
statement: The Modes of a declaration state which modes the service has; a process MAY still run a subset of them, selected by the mode option or STEGO_MODE. Checking MUST refuse a declaration whose Modes leave out a mode that its declared features need, with one fault at modes for each missing mode that names the mode and the features that need it: api, for a declaration with collections, commands or queries, which the service serves over HTTP or gRPC; worker, for a service on the runtime data path, whose outbox relay and audit sink run in the worker mode, and for a declared subscription, whose Kafka inbox runs in the worker mode (a declared worker is the fault of ST-DECL-INV71); controller, for a service on the runtime data path, whose audit anchor and maintenance jobs, and with workers and authorization the reconcile of the worker tuples (ST-SUP-RC35-OC13), run in the controller mode (a backfill is the fault of ST-DECL-INV61). STEGO MUST NOT add a mode itself. Omitted Modes mean all three. Decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation (review of PR #397, M1, 2026-11-17). The Kafka inbox: decision on ST-SUP-Q158, 2026-11-17.

title: A declaration gives each author-supplied setting
statement: Checking MUST refuse a declaration that gives no value for a setting that a component of its active set marks as author supplied in its config schema (ST-SUP-EN09), with one fault at overrides.<component>.<setting> for each such setting, which names the component and the setting. A component MUST mark as author supplied only a setting that every declaration with the component must give; a setting that only the running service gets, such as a connection string or an issuer, is not author supplied. Decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation (ST-DECL-Q05 (a), 2026-11-17).

title: A collection needs a component that serves it
statement: Each declared collection MUST be served by a component of the active set, and today only rest-api (ST-SUP-RC20) serves collections. Checking MUST refuse a collection of a service whose active set has no such component, naming the collection and the archetype, and the fault MUST tell that a service with no rest-api creates and changes rows through commands and reads them through queries. The orchestrator decided this under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17 (ST-SUP-Q155).

title: A reference held within an ancestor names a field that both rows share
statement: The within of a reference MUST be none or the name of a field that the entity declares and that the referenced entity declares too, each a required reference to the same entity or the scope field of a collection over that entity, and MUST NOT be the reference itself. Checking MUST refuse another within, naming the entity, the reference and the field. Checking MUST warn, and not refuse, about a reference without within when the entity and the referenced entity both declare a reference to the same entity, and the warning MUST tell how to declare within or within: none. The orchestrator decided this under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17 (ST-DECL-Q42).

title: A command or worker list is declared over fields of the entity
statement: A list of a command or a worker MUST name a list name that is unique in its command or worker, an entity that the command or worker writes, or that the worker reads, a filter of one to eight terms, each a declared field of that entity with one of the operators equals, not equals, less than, less than or equals, greater than, greater than or equals and is set, and a value that is a constant of the field type, the time of the run, or a parameter, and MAY name lock, only over an entity that the command or worker writes, which needs the Lock at most of the entity (ST-DECL-INV81). A parameter MUST have a name in lower snake case that is unique in its list, and its term MUST NOT be is set and MUST NOT give a constant or the time of the run; the fill gives the value of a parameter at call time, such as a field of the request or of the message. A term MAY instead name parent: true, only with the operator equals, on a reference field of the entity to an entity with a resource type; the fill then gives the loaded parent row at call time, so the referenced entity MUST be one that the command or worker writes, or that the worker reads. A list over a child entity, which has no resource type and a reference to an entity with a resource type, MUST have exactly one parent term, and a list over any other entity MUST have none; a child entity with more than one such reference MUST NOT have a list. An entity with no resource type and no such reference has no authorization of its rows, so its list reads the rows of the tenant, as its read does. Checking MUST refuse another list, naming the command or worker, the list and the term. The orchestrator decided this under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17 (ST-SUP-Q159, c; walkthrough 7, B1 and NB4). The parent term: the orchestrator decided this under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17 (security review of PR #416, M1). Reads: decision ST-SUP-Q186 (a), orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-18.

title: The admin relation of the provisioning is a relation of its resource type for the person subject
statement: When the tenant provisioning names an admin relation (ST-DECL-EN27), checking MUST refuse it unless the authorization schema declares it as a relation of the provisioning resource type that admits the subject type of subject_from_identity, and MUST refuse the relation tenant and every relation worker_<name>. A provisioning with no admin relation MUST be accepted as before. Walkthrough-7 NB2, decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17.

title: A subscription has a name of its own, and a service has at most eight
statement: A declaration MUST hold at most 8 subscriptions; checking MUST refuse a ninth with a fault that names the limit. A subscription's name MUST be in lower kebab case, at most 63 characters, unique among the subscriptions, and MUST NOT be the name of a command, a query, a worker or a controller, or a destination that the service reserves or that an active component declares, because the name is the destination of its messages and the stager of each of them. The orchestrator decided this under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17 (ST-SUP-Q158); the limit of 8 subscriptions, each read in a consumer group of its own, 2026-11-21 (ST-SUP-Q204).

title: A subscription takes declared change events of another service
statement: A subscription's source MUST be the name of a service in lower kebab case other than the declaring service, and its events MUST be 1 to 32 event kinds, each <source>.<entity in lower kebab case>.<created, updated or deleted> of that source, with no kind twice; checking MUST refuse each other source or kind with a fault at its path. The orchestrator decided this under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17 (ST-SUP-Q158).

title: One worker consumes a subscription, and only Kafka stages for it
statement: Exactly one worker of the declaration MUST have the trigger consumes <name> of each subscription, and it acts on each event with its own service account and declared writes; no command or worker MUST stage an effect for the destination of a subscription, whose messages come only from Kafka. Checking MUST refuse each other case with a fault that names the subscription. The orchestrator decided this under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-17 (ST-SUP-Q158).

title: An upsert key holds no optional field
statement: Each field of a collection's upsert key MUST be required: an optional field of the key binds NULL, which equals no row, and the unique key admits two rows whose field is NULL, so each upsert with that field empty would insert a new row (security review of PR #416, L4).

title: One successor, of the same component or of the one that took over its port
statement: A component digest MUST have at most one successor. The successor MUST be another digest of the same component, or a digest of the component that graduated to ga and took over the port the superseded component provided; in the second case the supersession MUST say that it needs a declaration change.

title: An installation replaces nothing
statement: An installation MUST refuse a result folder that already exists, and MUST NOT change what that folder holds.

title: A failed check leaves no installation
statement: When a digest check or a signature check fails, the installer MUST leave no result folder and no temporary download.

title: A compiler artifact exists only when two isolated builds agree
statement: A compiler artifact MUST be produced only when two builds from one commit in separate trees, homes and caches give byte-identical executables, module checksums and version records; a disagreement produces no artifact.

title: A release is one immutable tag per commit with four assets
statement: A compiler release MUST be published under the tag of its full commit, immutable, holding exactly the executable, its build record, SHA256SUMS and the signature bundle; a release or a tag MUST never be replaced, and a burned tag MUST be followed by a new commit and a new qualification.

title: Only the main-branch signing job signs, and only the bytes it fetched
statement: A compiler signature MUST come only from the signing job of a successful build of the pinned CI definition at the main branch, whether a push or a dispatch of that branch started the run; that job holds the only attestation permission, fetches the build's artifact by its immutable ID, and signs only after both digests match the build job's outputs.

title: A supersession's fail date follows the stage window
statement: A supersession's fail date MUST equal the successor's release date plus the window the registry states for the component's stage, alpha 0 months, beta 3 months, ga 6 months, doubled when taking the successor needs a declaration change, unless a platform engineer shortens it; a fail date MUST NOT be later than that.

title: Every need is stated
statement: Platform requirements MUST state, with its kind and shape, every secret, configuration value, backing store, topic, identity issuer, ingress, egress destination, cluster permission and pod security level that the service's components need, which are the nine kinds of ST-VO53.

title: Requirements hold no environment values
statement: Platform requirements MUST name needs and environment variables only, and MUST NOT hold a secret value, a host name, an address, a namespace or any other value that differs per environment, except the default and the allowed values that a component or the declaration states for a variable that is not secret, and the issuer of an identity issuer need that the declaration fixes, which are the same in every environment.

title: The CI file is one pinned call
statement: A delivery pipeline MUST hold only a call to its provider's shared pipeline and to the STEGO checks, each by a pinned reference, so that a change to the pipeline is a change to a pin.

title: The pins come from the registry
statement: A delivery pipeline's pinned references and trusted signer MUST come from the registry's ci-pipeline component, so one registry change and a regeneration move a service to a patched pipeline.

title: Every provider runs every STEGO check
